I'm now zeroing in on the role of '8' as an occluder, specifically considering the missing elements within the color '7' diamonds. In the training data, '8' seems to mask some points within the shape. Examining the first training example, I'm discovering that 8s appear to actively block specific diamond positions, resulting in a unique diamond formation of color 7. My focus is on determining how and when these occlusions occur. I think I'm close to a key insight!

Analyzing coordinates like (0,2), (1,1), (1,2) reveals a repeating pattern; specifically, a shape formed by a top point, with an expanding L-shape below. All instances of this template shape on the grid are completed, restoring any parts previously occluded by '8'. The occluder ('8') is effectively removed, transformed into the background. A visible part of a shape determines the position of that shape. I think I know how it works!

I'm now confirming the role of pure translations in the formation of shapes. I can see that all shapes of the same color are identical copies. Analyzing multiple examples confirms that all instances are simply translations of a single template. I'm double-checking different training examples and find no rotations or reflections. I think I'm close!

I've determined the foreground color is 9, the occluder is 8, and the grid size is 9x9. Now, I'm examining the shapes of color 9. Furthermore, I've located a similar inverted "U" arch on the right side at rows 3 to 5, using cols 6 to 8. I am searching for any other instances of the color 9 to see if any more shapes exist.
